title: Health Check: Nutrition Quiz
description: Race against the clock in this 20-question challenge about nutrition, fitness, and healthy living! From busting diet myths to understanding macronutrients, BMI, and the best foods in an Indian diet, discover what truly fuels your body and mind. Build answer streaks, beat the timer, and prove you know what it takes to stay healthy and sharp!
learning_objectives: Understand macronutrients (protein, carbohydrates, fats) and their roles in the body
Identify key vitamins and minerals and their food sources in an Indian diet
Learn the importance of hydration, BMI, and regular physical activity for students
Bust common myths about junk food, dieting, and nutrition fads
Recognize the connection between diet, mental health, and academic performance

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read each scenario-based question about health, nutrition, or fitness
Select your answer before the 12-second timer runs out
Earn 10 points per correct answer, plus streak bonuses for consecutive correct answers
Work through all 20 questions covering food groups, vitamins, Indian diet, fitness, and nutrition myths
Review your results to discover how well you understand what fuels your body and mind
tips: Read the full scenario before jumping to the options -- context clues often point to the right answer
Build answer streaks for extra points -- each consecutive correct answer earns a 5-point bonus
Think about your own daily meals and habits to connect the questions to real life
If unsure, eliminate the most obviously wrong options first to improve your chances

questions.question: Rahul eats only rice and dal for lunch and dinner every day. His nails have become brittle and he bruises easily. Which nutrient is he most likely missing?
questions.correct_answer: Vitamin C

questions.question: Which of these Indian foods is the richest source of protein per 100 grams?
questions.correct_answer: Paneer

questions.question: Your body uses three macronutrients as fuel. Which of the following is NOT a macronutrient?
questions.correct_answer: Vitamins

questions.question: Priya drinks only 2 glasses of water a day and often feels tired and gets headaches during class. A doctor would most likely advise her to:
options: Drink at least 8-10 glasses of water daily
Drink more tea and coffee instead
questions.correct_answer: Drink at least 8-10 glasses of water daily

questions.question: Amit's friend tells him that eating fat makes you fat, so he should avoid all fats. What is the correct response?
options: His friend is right -- all fats are bad and should be avoided completely
Only trans fats and excess saturated fats are harmful; healthy fats from nuts, ghee, and fish are essential
Fat has no role in the body so it does not matter either way
You only need fats if you exercise daily
questions.correct_answer: Only trans fats and excess saturated fats are harmful; healthy fats from nuts, ghee, and fish are essential

questions.question: Which vitamin does your body produce naturally when you spend time in sunlight?
questions.correct_answer: Vitamin D

questions.question: Sneha is training for her school athletics meet. Her coach asks her to increase her protein intake. Which Indian meal would best help her?
options: Chole (chickpea curry) with paneer paratha and a glass of lassi
White bread with jam and butter
questions.correct_answer: Chole (chickpea curry) with paneer paratha and a glass of lassi

questions.question: BMI stands for Body Mass Index. How is it calculated?
options: Weight in kg divided by height in metres squared
questions.correct_answer: Weight in kg divided by height in metres squared

questions.question: During exams, Kavya replaces meals with chips, biscuits, and energy drinks to save time studying. What is the most likely effect on her performance?
options: She will study better because she is saving time
Her concentration and memory will decline due to lack of proper nutrients
Energy drinks fully replace the need for balanced meals
Chips provide enough carbohydrates to fuel the brain
questions.correct_answer: Her concentration and memory will decline due to lack of proper nutrients

questions.question: Iron deficiency is common among Indian teenagers, especially girls. Which of these foods is the best vegetarian source of iron?
questions.correct_answer: Spinach (palak) and jaggery (gur)

questions.question: Arjun wants to gain muscle for his basketball team. He starts drinking raw eggs every morning because he saw it in a movie. What should his coach tell him?
options: Raw eggs are the best protein source -- keep going
Raw eggs can carry Salmonella bacteria; cooked eggs, dal, and paneer are safer protein sources
Eggs have no protein, so it is pointless
He should only eat chicken to build muscle
questions.correct_answer: Raw eggs can carry Salmonella bacteria; cooked eggs, dal, and paneer are safer protein sources

questions.question: The Glycemic Index (GI) measures how quickly a food raises blood sugar. Which of these Indian staples has the LOWEST glycemic index?
questions.correct_answer: Whole wheat roti

questions.question: How many minutes of moderate physical activity per day does the WHO recommend for teenagers aged 12-17?
questions.correct_answer: 60 minutes

questions.question: Meera is a vegetarian and has been diagnosed with Vitamin B12 deficiency. Which food should she add to her diet?
questions.correct_answer: Milk, curd, and paneer

questions.question: A typical plate from the 'My Plate' balanced diet model should have the largest portion filled with:
options: Dairy products like milk and curd
questions.correct_answer: Vegetables and fruits

questions.question: Rohan skips breakfast every day because he wants to lose weight. What does research say about skipping breakfast?
options: It is the fastest way to lose weight and is perfectly healthy
Skipping breakfast can slow metabolism and lead to overeating later, making weight management harder
Breakfast has no effect on weight at all
Skipping breakfast only matters for adults, not teenagers
questions.correct_answer: Skipping breakfast can slow metabolism and lead to overeating later, making weight management harder

questions.question: During a cricket match on a hot day, a player is sweating heavily. Besides water, what does the body lose through sweat that needs to be replaced?
questions.correct_answer: Electrolytes like sodium and potassium

questions.question: Ananya notices that eating a heavy biryani lunch makes her sleepy in the afternoon class. What is the most likely scientific reason?
options: The body diverts more blood to the digestive system after a large, carb-heavy meal, reducing alertness
It is purely psychological and has nothing to do with food
questions.correct_answer: The body diverts more blood to the digestive system after a large, carb-heavy meal, reducing alertness

questions.question: Research shows a strong connection between gut health and mental health. Which traditional Indian food is a natural probiotic that supports gut health?
options: Homemade curd (dahi) and fermented idli batter
questions.correct_answer: Homemade curd (dahi) and fermented idli batter

questions.question: Vikram wants to plan a balanced post-workout snack. He just finished a 45-minute football practice. Which option gives him the best combination of protein and carbohydrates for recovery?
options: A packet of chips and a cold drink
A banana with a handful of roasted chana (chickpeas) and a glass of buttermilk (chaas)
Only a protein shake with no carbohydrates
questions.correct_answer: A banana with a handful of roasted chana (chickpeas) and a glass of buttermilk (chaas)

glossary_terms.definition: A numerical value calculated from your weight and height (weight in kg divided by height in metres squared) used as a screening tool to indicate whether a person is underweight, normal weight, overweight, or obese. For teenagers, BMI is interpreted using age- and gender-specific percentiles.

The three major nutrients your body needs in large amounts for energy and growth: carbohydrates (4 cal/g), proteins (4 cal/g), and fats (9 cal/g). A balanced Indian thali typically provides all three through roti (carbs), dal (protein), and ghee (fat).

Vitamins and minerals that the body needs in small quantities but are essential for proper functioning. Examples include iron (found in spinach and jaggery), Vitamin C (found in amla and citrus fruits), and calcium (found in milk and ragi). Deficiencies can cause serious health problems.

The set of chemical processes in your body that convert food into energy. Your metabolic rate determines how many calories you burn at rest. Factors like age, muscle mass, physical activity, and even meal timing (like eating breakfast) can influence your metabolism.

A ranking system from 0 to 100 that measures how quickly a food raises blood sugar levels after eating. Low-GI foods (like whole wheat roti, oats, and dal) release sugar slowly and provide sustained energy, while high-GI foods (like white rice and white bread) cause rapid spikes and crashes.

cultural_context: India's healthcare system faces unique pressures — with a doctor-patient ratio far below WHO recommendations and a growing burden of lifestyle diseases. Health Check: Nutrition Quiz builds the analytical and decision-making skills needed by India's future health leaders.
